results.statement: For independent cap-one U,V, fixed a!=0,b,t, the density of aU^2+bU+2tV is bounded by min{1/(2|t|), sqrt(2/(|a||t|))}. If T has density cap sqrt(2)/gamma then averaging this envelope gives <=6 e^(-1/3)(|a|gamma^2)^(-1/3).

In Q=2(X0+ell.X_L)(g.X_L)+d(beta.X_L)^2, beta.g=0, ||beta||=1, if g_i=0 then ||p_Q||inf<=6e^(-1/3)(|d|gamma^2 beta_i^2)^(-1/3), with arbitrary dense/source-entangled ell. In the target-normalized heavy branch hD>=1/5 and q_i=beta_i^2>1/2, this is <9.262319472. Continuity not claimed.

If L=J disjoint_union K, g_K=beta_K=0, ell_J=a g+b beta, then S=X0+ell_K.X_K is genuinely independent of (g.X_J,beta.X_J), LPP gives pair cap <=2/gamma, and QFORM-CAPPED-SCALAR-DEPENDENT-PAIR-v1 yields ||p_Q||inf<=3*4^(2/3)(|d|gamma^2)^(-1/3), hence <=12.926608141 when hD>=1/5.

For G=(X1+X2)/sqrt(2), W=(X1-X2)/sqrt(2), Q_theta=2(X0+theta W)G+X3^2, the physical spectrum is {-sqrt(1+theta^2),0,1,sqrt(1+theta^2)}. G,W need not be independent. The zero-edge theorem gives a whole-line bound 6e^(-1/3)=4.299187864 for every theta; pinned e5f ruled-surface theorem separately gives p(t)<=pi sqrt(2) for a.e. t>=0.
